paragraphs.text: Towashi is the main city of modern day Kamigawa .

Towashi is characterized by looming skyscrapers, large neon signs, and vibrant cherry trees. It was built in a cleared-out part of the Jukai Forest . It is the seat of Imperial power. Now, kami and humans alike live among its towering skyscrapers. The streets are always packed, no matter the time of day. Its prime location along the coast makes it a hub for commerce, and its proximity to the forest provides shelter from the elements. Arcades make up a notable portion of the city's economy. Hovering lanterns and neon lights brighten a lower city that would otherwise be drowned in shadows throughout the day, and those same lights transform the city at night into a beacon of dazzling colors.
Towashi is famous for its Lantern Festival, celebrated by humans and kami alike.

At the dawn of the era now referred to as the Modern Age, the city of Towashi was undergoing a period of rapid expansion to support its growing population. Diverse communities of Moonfolk , nezumi , humans , and akki were living side by side, interacting and blending in ways that would have been unimaginable in earlier times. As Towashi extended its borders, it began encroaching upon the Jukai Forest , with vast numbers of trees being cut down to make way for new construction. This expansion displaced many of the forest's native kami , who, angered by the destruction of their home, rose from the forest depths to retaliate, damaging buildings and casting curses upon those responsible for the deforestation.

The emperor at the time finally intervened when an attack by the kami, and the Towashi builders' subsequent retaliation, threatened to upend all the peaceful relations between mortals and kami once more. He brokered an agreement that the city would halt further growth into the forest. Meanwhile, the kami would not attack the city or intrude upon their planning. The city builders could continue to develop any land they had already started building on, with one exception: they were forbidden from cutting down Boseiju, which had fallen into the city's domain during the construction and fighting. Furthermore, Jukai Forest was now closed to all mortals without permission from the kami.
Unable to expand outward, Towashi was forced to grow upwards instead. Skyscrapers filled the city, and Boseiju was soon lost within the skyline.

But then the millennia-old tree, which had lain quiet for so long, began to grow once again. It grew so large and so tall that it came to eclipse even the tallest structures surrounding it. Builders attempted to match its height, but for every new "tallest structure" constructed, Boseiju grew even more. Boseiju's message was clear: the city might be standing on this ground now, but the forest refused to let anyone forget who had been there first. Today, Boseiju is the largest structure in Towashi, its spreading branches casting a near-permanent shadow over much of Towashi.

During the New Phyrexian Invasion , the compleated planeswalker Tamiyo led the assault on the plane at Towashi, making the Boseiju District the invasion's prime target. The tree itself was corrupted by Tamiyo , who burst it apart, causing glistening oil to run from between the splinters.
Far Corner is a neighborhood on the border between Towashi City and Jukai forest. In the past, it was a village belonging to the Jukai forest.
The Imperial Palace complex, a secondary palace for the Emperor.

The Towashi Undercity - the part of Towashi located on the ground, wedged between the shadows of Boseiju and Towashi's skyscrapers. The Bent Alley Dragon's Well is a venerated, protected meeting site where the heads of different gangs meet to hash out disagreements and make formal treaties. One of the lowest sections of the Undercity, an area forever shielded from the sunlight by a matrix of bridges that serviced those who worked and lived in Towashi's skyscrapers. It also housed a safe house for the Infinite Consortium .
